subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I need to write a single TypeScript module using only the documented SDK functions available—builder methods like joint, chain, sweep, part, stick, cards, extrude, membrane, spike, along, ring, decal, surface, plus helpers like paint, spots, stripes, countershade, svg, rng, frame, line, aim, lerp, and mid.

I'm figuring out the likely signatures since I don't have exhaustive docs: joints probably take a name and options like at/aim/dir/up/parent, with parent referencing another joint; chains likely build joints along a path; and sweep probably takes a path, radius, and style options to generate tube-like geometry. I'll keep the implementation modest and stick to the safest, most clearly-documented calls to avoid relying on unverified API behavior.

I'm sorting out the `aim`/`dir` parameter order for `b.part` and assuming cone geometry's default +Y axis orients toward the aim point, with parts attaching to the heaviest bone automatically when unspecified. Now I'm settling on overall phoenix proportions, roughly 2.2 units in height.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton layout: body root joint, neck chain curving upward from chest to head, with coordinates set along a +Z forward axis for head/tail placement, wingspan around 3.6m total. I'm uncertain whether `b.chain` accepts a role option, so I'm considering using direct joints and sweep primitives for the neck instead as a safer fallback.

For the tail, I'm planning a chain of joints descending and extending backward, then attaching feather blades at points along that chain using frame or aim-based orientation—leaning toward computing explicit aim points from known coordinates since the frame-axis convention is unclear. Next I'll move on to designing the wings.

Now I'm working out the wing skeleton as a chain of shoulder-to-wingtip joints, then figuring out how to extrude flat feather outlines in the plane of the wing using spanwise and up-ish directions as local axes for a tapered, flame-like shape.

Primaries get colored by position along the wing—crimson near the body, shifting through red-orange, amber, to gold at the tips—using a shared palette and some jitter for variation. I'm building the left wing as a function with a sign parameter so I can mirror it to generate the right wing symmetrically.

Simplifying the wing shape to a four-point polyline from shoulder to tip (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip), then interpolating along these segments to place each feather's base point and compute its outward-and-drooping direction.
